statement: In the AutoCAD mobile app, FIND must offer an editor bar to enter search text (with wildcards), choose the search scope, set which object kinds and matching rules apply, and navigate hits with next/previous controls that zoom to each instance and display the number found.
notes: Added from help page "FIND (Command)"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: In the mobile app run FIND for 'PUMP' in a drawing with three matching texts, assert the count shows 3 and tapping next zooms to each in turn.

statement: The mobile app must accept drawings opened from local storage, email or messaging apps and upload them to the user's web and mobile cloud storage (also reachable by web upload or SAVETOWEBANDMOBILE), requiring a connection and syncing emailed drawings to the device for offline work.
notes: Added from help page "About Uploading Files to AutoCAD Web"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Open a DWG from an email attachment in the mobile app, assert it appears in cloud storage and is available offline afterward.

statement: The mobile app must provide a file manager home screen to open, upload, download, rename, delete, move and duplicate files, create folders and new Metric or Imperial drawings (saved in 2018 format), connect to storage, and download files for offline use, with folder operations limited to its own cloud storage.
notes: Added from help page "File Management"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Tap New Drawing > Metric, assert a 2018-format drawing is created; create a folder, move the file into it, and duplicate it and assert the copy lands next to the original.

statement: The mobile app must offer a Send a Copy option that shares a copy of the drawing through any available client (email, messenger, AirDrop), without packaging attached references.
notes: Added from help page "Send a Copy"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Choose Options > Send a Copy for a drawing with an xref, send via email and assert the attachment is only the DWG without the xref.

statement: The mobile app must connect to cloud storage providers (Microsoft OneDrive, Google Drive, Dropbox, Box, Forma Data Management) through the Add Source action and sign-in, allow several accounts for each provider, let drawings there be viewed, edited and saved, and allow providers to be disconnected.
notes: Added from help page "Cloud Storage Providers"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Add a Dropbox source, open and save a drawing in it and assert the cloud copy updates; add a second Dropbox account and assert both are listed.

statement: The mobile app must download drawings automatically when opened or on request (Download to offline) and sync changes made offline when the connection returns.
notes: Added from help page "Working Offline"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Open a drawing, go offline, edit it, reconnect and assert the cloud copy contains the edit.

statement: The mobile app must provide Plot to PDF (also via PLOT) with paper size, orientation, what to plot (current display in model space, or current/all layouts in paper space), a plot style choice from five options, scale to fit in model space and 1:1 in paper space.
notes: Added from help page "Plot to PDF"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Plot a layout at A4 landscape with monochrome style and assert a one-page PDF at 1:1 scale with black-only linework; plot model space and assert it scales to fit.

statement: The web and mobile apps must let users create traces from the Traces panel, close them with a check mark, block saving while a trace is open, edit only their own traces (others' are view-only), rename, delete or remove contributions, share traces implicitly with the drawing, while the desktop app shows them view-only.
notes: Added from help page "Working With Trace"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: In the mobile app create a trace, draw a line, close it and assert the trace is stored with the drawing; assert another user's trace cannot be edited.

statement: The web and mobile apps must support Trace as a layer of proposed changes on a drawing without altering it, sent to collaborators who are notified in desktop, supported only in drawing formats 2010 or later and not DXF.
notes: Added from help page "About Trace"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Create a trace in mobile, save to DXF and assert traces are not preserved while saving as 2018 DWG preserves them.

statement: The mobile app must provide a bottom toolbar with Select, Measure, Draw and Annotate categories and a command line with auto-complete suggestions, showing command prompts and option buttons while a command is active.
notes: Added from help page "Toolbar"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Type LI in the command line and assert LINE is suggested; tap Draw > Circle and assert the 'Specify center point' prompt with 3P, 2P and Ttr options appears.

statement: The mobile app must support point specification by dragging the cursor and tapping to confirm for draw commands (LINE, POLYLINE, RECTANGLE, ARC, CIRCLE) and for base and second points in modify commands, ending with Esc.
notes: Added from help page "Drawing and Modifying Objects"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Run LINE, drag to a point and tap to confirm twice, press Esc, assert one line exists; select it, run MOVE with drag-and-tap points, and assert it moved by that displacement.

statement: The mobile app must provide a Views palette that switches between model space and the layouts of a drawing, which can be viewed but not created in the mobile app.
notes: Added from help page "Views"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Open a drawing with two layouts, use the Views palette to switch to layout 2 and assert that layout becomes active.

statement: The mobile app must attach DWG or image (JPG, PNG, BMP, GIF) external references via the External References palette or ATTACH, picking the file from the file manager, photo library or camera and then prompting for insertion point and scale factor, keeping references linked to the source.
notes: Added from help page "Attach an External Reference"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Run ATTACH, pick a PNG, give an insertion point and scale 2 and assert the image reference is placed at 2x scale in the Xrefs list.

statement: The mobile app must support touch navigation: two-finger drag to pan (one-finger when no command is active), pinch to zoom, and Zoom Extents from the header or a two-finger double-tap.
notes: Added from help page "Pan and Zoom"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Simulate a two-finger drag and assert the view pans; simulate a pinch-out and assert zoom changes; double-tap with two fingers and assert the view equals zoom extents.

statement: The mobile app must provide a Layers palette to create layers, turn off all layers, and modify a layer by setting it current, turning it on or off and changing other properties, so the user can hide objects by function.
notes: Added from help page "Layers"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Create layer 'WALLS', set it current, draw a line, turn the layer off and assert the line is hidden.

statement: The mobile app must provide a Blocks palette for inserting existing block definitions at a specified insertion point, while block creation is unavailable on mobile and left to the web or desktop app.
notes: Added from help page "Blocks"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Tap a block in the Blocks palette, specify an insertion point and assert a block reference is created there; assert no block-create command is available.

statement: The mobile app must provide an Xrefs palette listing DWG and image (JPG, JPEG, PNG, GIF, BMP) references, resolving paths from the parent folder or defined path, and allowing a missing or existing reference to be replaced by tapping it and choosing a file.
notes: Added from help page "External References Manager"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Open a drawing with a missing xref, tap it in the Xrefs palette, choose the file and assert the reference resolves and displays.

statement: The mobile app must provide a Properties palette listing key property settings (such as color and linetype) of selected objects that can be edited by tapping fields.
notes: Added from help page "Properties"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Select a line, open Properties, change its color to red and assert the line is red.

statement: The mobile app must provide MEASURE with Distance (two points), Angle (arc, circle or two lines) and Area (sequence of points with perimeter), plus a quick mode showing distances and angles from rays through the tapped point, with object snaps for precision.
notes: Added from help page "Measure"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Measure the distance between two snapped points on a 3-4-5 triangle and assert 5; choose Area, tap four rectangle corners and assert the correct area and perimeter.

statement: The mobile app must offer a Settings menu, usable during a command, for object snap on/off and modes, object snap tracking, polar tracking with increment angle, drawing units (linear, angular, insertion scale) and grid options.
notes: Added from help page "Drawing Settings"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Turn on polar tracking at 30 degrees and the grid, draw a line and assert it snaps to a 30-degree angle with the grid visible.
